positions.as_written: Use the sagittal proton density or T2 weighted sequence to assess it.
Confirm a round low signal structure by following it across slices before calling it a loose body.
Compare thickness with the contralateral knee where a study is available, rather than against a single quoted figure.
Read the posterior capsule on the same slices.
Use the normal study as the reference for the contralateral comparison rather than as a set of absolute values.
Read continuity, uniformity and calibre as three separate observations.
Assess the posterior capsule and the fat plane on the same study as the ligament.
Measure the distance from the femoral footprint to the articular margin where a tunnel is planned, rather than estimating it at operation.
Document the presence of the meniscofemoral ligaments.
Avoid reading a curved ligament in an extended knee as a healed injury.
